In distributed event streaming architectures, building a robust data processing pipeline requires mastering Kafka Consumers, their continuous poll loop, appropriate offset commit strategies, and handling consumer group rebalancing. The consumer is not merely a passive listener; it maintains an active, stateful TCP connection to the cluster, pulling batches of records via the poll loop. Every consumer belongs to a consumer group, which enables horizontal scaling and fault-tolerant stream processing by dividing partition ownership among its members.

The poll loop is the heart of the consumer runtime. It is a synchronous method invocation (poll()) that serves a dual purpose: it fetches records from assigned partitions and acts as a heartbeat mechanism to the group coordinator. If the application logic takes longer than max.poll.interval.ms to process a batch and call poll() again, the coordinator assumes the consumer is dead and triggers a rebalancing event. Managing how and when offsets are committed—whether automatically in the background or manually for precise, at-least-once or at-most-once delivery semantics—dictates the consistency of your downstream systems.

Rebalancing is the protocol-driven reallocation of partition assignments across the members of a consumer group. It occurs when new consumers join, existing consumers leave or crash, or topic metadata changes. During a rebalance, processing halts entirely while the group stops-the-world to negotiate new ownership, making low-latency rebalance listeners and efficient cooperative sticky assignors critical for minimizing application downtime.

Potential out-of-order offset overwrites if retries aren't carefully managed

items: The poll loop relies on a internal fetcher that buffers records locally. When poll(Duration timeout) is called, it returns records from this local buffer, and asynchronously triggers the next network fetch in the background.

Consumer group rebalancing is orchestrated by a designated broker acting as the Group Coordinator. It uses JoinGroup and SyncGroup heartbeats to coordinate state transitions between the consumer instances and assignors.

Cooperative Sticky Assignor minimizes partition movement during a rebalance by revoking only the specific partitions that need to move, avoiding the stop-the-world partition drop of the older Range or Eager assignors.

parsed_answer.content: A classic production failure mode is the 'livelock' or continuous rebalance storm caused by long-running business logic inside the poll loop. If your database write takes 6 minutes and max.poll.interval.ms is set to 5 minutes (default 300000ms), the consumer will drop out of the group, trigger a rebalance, rejoin, and immediately drop out again. Always offload heavy processing to a thread pool executor, pause consumption on those partitions using consumer.pause(), or tune your polling intervals appropriately.
